articles.title: A Systematic Review of New, Enhanced Surveillance Systems and Methodologies for Zoonotic Influenza Viruses in Animals and Human-Animal Interface.

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

en.research_question: The authors aimed to evaluate recent developments in monitoring techniques for animal and cross-species influenza viruses to determine which innovations warrant broader application and which areas require further investigation.
en.study_design: This work follows a systematic review framework guided by PRISMA standards, synthesizing data from 164 selected publications out of an initial search yielding 7,490 records.
en.population_setting: The scope encompasses global efforts to track influenza strains circulating among wildlife, livestock, and humans, with particular attention to interaction zones where spillover events occur.
en.main_findings: The analysis identifies multiple technological improvements alongside persistent structural deficiencies in monitoring networks. Current documentation indicates that numerous regions operate without robust cross-sectoral tracking systems, resulting in incomplete estimates of infection prevalence. Priority actions emphasize integrating multi-sectoral datasets, standardizing new testing tools, scaling passive sampling strategies, and aligning technical upgrades with regulatory decision-making.
en.public_health_relevance: Strengthening coordinated monitoring frameworks is presented as essential for reducing seasonal illness impacts and mitigating future outbreak threats through improved diagnostic readiness and targeted research funding.
en.limitations: The evaluation relies exclusively on indexed academic publications, which may overlook operational field data or reflect uneven research investment across different geographic areas. Additionally, the focus on a seven-year window restricts historical context for long-term trend analysis.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication offers a consolidated perspective on methodological evolution within cross-species pathogen tracking initiatives. It contextualizes recent scholarly contributions toward standardized data collection and policy alignment without referencing active epidemiological dashboards or real-time transmission metrics.

articles.title: Intranasal and intramuscular H5-Matrix-M nanoparticle vaccines protects against highly pathogenic H5N1 influenza virus in mice
articles.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

en.research_question: The investigation evaluates whether a Matrix-M-adjuvanted nanoparticle vaccine can generate protective immune responses against an emerging H5N1 strain when delivered via nasal or injection routes.
en.study_design: A controlled animal experiment utilizing two mouse cohorts, one unexposed and one previously administered a seasonal influenza formulation, followed by targeted viral challenge.
en.population_setting: Laboratory mice subjected to either baseline conditions or prior seasonal influenza immunization before receiving the experimental nanoparticle construct.
en.main_findings: Both delivery methods triggered substantial antibody production and prevented mortality following lethal exposure. Previously immunized animals required only a single booster dose to achieve comparable defense, while nasal application resulted in lower viral detection within the upper respiratory tract compared to injections.
en.public_health_relevance: The data indicate that this adjuvanted nanoparticle approach may circumvent interference from existing seasonal influenza antibodies, highlighting its potential utility in pandemic response strategies.
en.limitations: Findings are restricted to murine models and do not account for human physiological differences, extended durability of protection, or adverse event profiling.
en.gids_interpretation: This record documents early-stage experimental work on a specific adjuvanted platform targeting an evolving avian influenza lineage, offering contextual background for monitoring vaccine innovation trajectories rather than active epidemiological tracking.

zh.research_question: 评估含重组H5血凝素的纳米颗粒疫苗经不同途径接种后，在基础及既往接触季节性流感的小鼠体内诱导的免疫原性与保护效力。
zh.study_design: 采用小鼠动物实验设计，对比鼻内与肌内两种给药方案，涵盖未暴露组与季节性流感预免疫组，并在病毒攻毒后记录免疫指标与感染情况。
zh.population_setting: 实验室环境下的健康小鼠，以及预先接受季节性流感疫苗免疫的小鼠群体。
zh.main_findings: 两种接种途径均能激发显著的结合抗体与中和抗体反应，并有效抵御致死性H5N1病毒攻击。在已预免疫的小鼠中，鼻内给药在上呼吸道检测到的突破性感染数量少于肌内注射。
zh.public_health_relevance: 针对近期高致病性H5N1病毒跨物种传播引发的公共卫生担忧，该研究为应对可能具备大流行潜力的新型流感病毒提供了候选疫苗技术路径。
zh.limitations: 研究仅基于小鼠模型开展，其免疫应答特征与保护效果外推至人类群体时需谨慎评估。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献聚焦于应对特定进化分支流感病毒的预防策略，属于疫苗研发与病原学监测交叉领域的学术探讨，为相关技术路线的演进提供了参考依据。

articles.title: Transmission, Pathological and Clinical Manifestations of Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A Virus in Mammals with Emphasis on H5N1 Clade 2.3.4.4b.

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

en.research_question: This review investigates the transmission patterns, disease pathology, and clinical symptoms associated with highly pathogenic avian influenza A virus H5N1 clade 2.3.4.4b in mammalian hosts, with particular attention to central nervous system involvement.
en.study_design: The authors performed a narrative review that synthesized previously documented case reports to characterize infection patterns across distinct mammalian categories.
en.population_setting: The analysis focuses on naturally infected terrestrial wildlife, marine species, and dairy cattle, with documented cross-species spillover events concentrated in European and American regions.
en.main_findings: Clinical presentations vary by host group, showing respiratory and neurological symptoms in marine animals alongside lethargy and neurological deficits in land-dwelling species. Tissue damage predominantly targets the lungs and brain in wildlife, whereas gastrointestinal and mammary structures are primarily affected in livestock. Elevated viral concentrations within neural tissue highlight a strong neurological preference, while emerging observations suggest possible direct animal-to-animal and parent-to-offspring spread.
en.public_health_relevance: The demonstrated capacity for cross-species infection and potential intermammalian transmission highlights ongoing risks for human exposure and reinforces the importance of systematic monitoring to track viral evolution in animal reservoirs.
en.limitations: The precise biological mechanisms enabling central nervous system entry remain unverified, with several theoretical pathways still under discussion. Furthermore, the conclusions rely entirely on compiled observational reports rather than controlled experimental investigations.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication situates cross-species viral ecology within broader One Health frameworks by cataloging host-specific disease signatures and highlighting the scientific value of coordinated tracking systems for emerging infectious agents.

zh.research_question: 本文旨在系统梳理高致病性禽流感H5N1 2.3.4.4b亚型在自然感染哺乳动物中的传播途径、病理改变及临床表现，并重点评估其中枢神经系统受累特征。
zh.study_design: 该文献属于同行评议的综述文章，通过归纳现有病例报告来总结特定病毒株在不同哺乳动物类群中的感染规律。
zh.population_setting: 研究对象主要来源于欧洲与美洲地区报告的多种自然感染哺乳动物，按生态习性划分为陆生动物、海洋哺乳动物及奶牛三大类别。
zh.main_findings: 临床观察显示海洋哺乳动物常出现神经与呼吸道症状，陆生动物以神经异常和嗜睡为主，奶牛则主要表现为胃肠道与乳腺病变。免疫组化与分子检测证实脑组织内病毒载量显著升高，提示该毒株具备较强的神经趋向性。此外，文中记录了哺乳动物间传播及垂直传播的相关证据。
zh.public_health_relevance: 新型传播途径的发现提示该病毒在人畜共患及大流行潜力方面存在不确定性，强调了持续追踪宿主范围内病毒演化特征的必要性。
zh.limitations: 中枢神经系统入侵的具体路径目前仍缺乏明确界定。作为基于既往文献的综述，其分析结果受限于原始报道数据的完整性与一致性。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该研究为学术性综述，主要提供特定禽流感病毒株在哺乳动物宿主中的已知感染图谱与传播背景，可作为相关领域文献检索与背景知识构建的参考依据。

articles.title: Biosecurity Uptake and Perceived Risk of Avian Influenza Among People in Contact With Birds.

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

en.research_question: What are the current adoption rates of protective practices and how do individuals involved in avian husbandry perceive zoonotic disease threats?
en.study_design: A cross-sectional survey utilizing standardized questionnaires administered over a three-month period.
en.population_setting: Two hundred twenty-five respondents located in the United Kingdom who maintain regular contact with poultry or other avian species.
en.main_findings: Post-contact hand cleaning emerged as the predominant safety protocol, followed by the use of chemical footbaths. Daily interactions with larger bird counts increased the likelihood of employing various protective gear categories. While concerns regarding viral impacts on animal welfare were pronounced, especially among large-scale operators, apprehension about personal infection remained uniformly low across all participant groups.
en.public_health_relevance: The observed gap between routine animal-focused protocols and human-directed precautions suggests opportunities for targeted educational outreach. Understanding these behavioral patterns can help shape communication strategies that address specific compliance obstacles within high-exposure demographics.
en.limitations: Reliance on self-reported survey responses from a single geographic region may introduce reporting bias and limit broader applicability.
en.gids_interpretation: This publication supplies foundational behavioral metrics and awareness benchmarks useful for contextualizing avian influenza preparedness discussions within academic and policy literature. It functions as a static reference point for tracking historical compliance trends rather than indicating active epidemiological monitoring or real-time threat escalation.

zh.research_question: 本研究旨在调查英国接触鸟类人群的生物安全措施采用情况及其对禽流感的风险认知，重点关注预防跨物种传播的相关实践。
zh.study_design: 该研究采用横断面问卷调查设计，于2024年5月至7月期间收集数据。
zh.population_setting: 研究对象为英国境内225名日常与鸟类存在接触的人员。
zh.main_findings: 接触鸟类后洗手是最普遍的措施，其次为鞋底消毒。接触鸟类数量越多，使用个人防护装备的概率越高。受访者普遍认为禽流感对禽类健康威胁较大，但对其自身健康风险认知较低，表明现有措施主要侧重于控制禽间传播而非人畜共患。
zh.public_health_relevance: 结果揭示了当前生物安全实践在阻断人畜共患传播方面的局限性，提示公共卫生部门需针对特定人群制定干预策略，以改善防护措施的实际应用效果。
zh.limitations: 研究依赖自我报告问卷且样本局限于单一国家，横断面设计难以确立因果关系或评估行为的长期演变。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献从同一健康视角补充了禽流感人畜共患传播链中的人类行为学数据，有助于完善相关疾病传播动力学模型中的风险认知维度。

articles.title: Role and Contribution of Serological Surveillance in Animals and Exposed Humans to the Study of Zoonotic Influenza Disease Epidemiology: A Scoping Review.

diseases.name_zh: 人感染高致病性禽流感

zh.research_question: 该综述旨在梳理2017年至2024年间全球关于动物及暴露人群血清学监测的研究现状，并评估其在人畜共患流感流行病学研究中的作用与方法进展。
zh.study_design: 研究采用范围综述设计，遵循PRISMA-ScR指南检索PubMed数据库，纳入2017年1月至2024年3月发表的相关英文同行评审文献。
zh.population_setting: 纳入数据涵盖33个国家的25种动物物种，其中家禽与生猪的血清学调查最为集中，同时涉及部分伴侣动物、野生哺乳动物及职业暴露人类群体。
zh.main_findings: 最终筛选出90项符合条件的研究，结果显示跨物种传播界面及非经济动物的监测资料相对匮乏。新兴的多重检测与纳米抗体技术虽具应用潜力，但在实际部署中仍面临操作与推广障碍。
zh.public_health_relevance: 将血清学监测更深度地整合至“同一健康”策略中，有望强化高风险区域与人兽交界地的早期预警能力与大流行防范准备。
zh.limitations: 本综述仅依赖单一电子数据库且限定英文文献，未开展正式的质量评价，且纳入的各项研究之间存在显著的异质性。
zh.gids_interpretation: 该文献系统归纳了现有血清学监测研究的地理与物种分布特征，揭示了当前数据覆盖的盲区，可为后续监测网络优化提供背景参考，但不代表实时疫情追踪结果。

en.research_question: The authors sought to catalog worldwide research on antibody tracking for zoonotic influenza across animal reservoirs and at-risk human cohorts over a seven-year period.
en.study_design: A systematic scoping review was conducted using PRISMA-ScR protocols to evaluate peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed.
en.population_setting: Eligible records covered thirty-three nations and documented twenty-five distinct animal taxa, with particular emphasis on agricultural livestock and workers with direct animal contact.
en.main_findings: Analysis of ninety qualifying papers demonstrated that current antibody monitoring predominantly targets poultry and pigs, leaving wildlife and companion species significantly understudied. While advanced testing formats such as multiplex and nanobody assays emerged, practical adoption continues to encounter operational hurdles.
en.public_health_relevance: Expanding antibody-based monitoring programs across interconnected health sectors may improve early identification of cross-species viral circulation and strengthen global outbreak readiness.
en.limitations: The authors note that restricting searches to one repository, excluding non-English works, omitting formal study quality evaluation, and encountering high methodological diversity constrain the review's comprehensiveness.
en.gids_interpretation: This work functions as a bibliometric and methodological inventory of historical antibody tracking initiatives for avian and swine influenza, offering context on regional coverage and technical evolution without referencing active outbreak monitoring.
